text:
sara: Heads-up everyone — new temporary policy rolling out today: Emergency dependent-care stipend for unplanned school/daycare closures + optional On-Call Recovery Days for engineers who cover extra shifts.

sara: TL;DR — stipend available up to 4x per rolling year (region-adjusted amount), effective 2025-07-01. On-Call Recovery Days: 1 paid recovery day per full on-call week where you exceed your baseline incident count. Full details and examples in the handbook: https://redwoodinference.internal/handbook/people/emergency-dependents

jordan: Awesome — quick q: if my kid's school closed last month and I purchased backup care, can I submit for the stipend retroactively?

sara: Short answer: generally no for the blanket rollout. We can make case-by-case exceptions for recent events if you missed the window — file a ticket to people-ops-case@redwood.com with receipts and a short note. We'll review within 5 business days.

dan: Who approves the recovery days? My team rotates coverage and I want to avoid people double-booking time off.

sara: Approvals stay with your manager; People Ops will do spot checks. Process: engineer submits recovery day in HR portal with reason "On-Call Recovery" and manager approves. If >2 consecutive recovery days requested, loop in People Ops for coordination.

mike: Are contractors eligible? And how is the stipend paid for international folks (EUR/GBP/etc)?

sara: Contractors not eligible for stipend, but managers can grant unpaid VTO as needed. For full-time employees the stipend amount is converted to local currency and listed on the handbook page (see "Regional amounts" table). It will appear as a separate payroll reimbursement line.

eliz: Thanks for doing this — super helpful for parents. :heart:

policydoc-bot: Updated policy doc published: /handbook/people/emergency-dependents (v1.0) — effective 2025-07-01. Change log: stipend + on-call recovery rules.

jordan: One tiny nit — can we add expense code for bookkeeping? makes approvals easier.

sara: Great call. Expense code is `DEP-STIP` for stipend reimbursements, and `ONC-REC` for on-call recovery payroll adjustments. Add those to your expense notes.

mike: Noted. Will forward to team and update our on-call runbook.

sara: We'll host a 30-min drop-in tomorrow at 11:00 PT to walk through scenarios and answer Qs. If you can't make it, drop questions here or DM me. :calendar:
